marks.gloss_en: דתניא, רבי יוחנן בן יוסף: שחטה ואחר כך הקדישה -- חייב לכסות, שכבר נתחייב בכיסוי קודם שיבא לידי הקדש (kind svara: the marker is a bare דתניא)
מעיקרא איחייב ליה בשילוח מקמי דאקדשה (= p_kvar_nitchayev_kodem_hekdesh), as R' Yochanan b. Yosef's baraita on covering the blood
a case where he lifted the mother, consecrated her, and returned her
מאי טעמא? דלא מיתמר ליה בלא עלי
Rav Hamnuna: all agree with regard to valuations that even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable
אמר ליה רבי שמעון בן לקיש: וכיון שמרדה פקעה לה קדושתה! -- once the hen rebelled, its sanctity lapsed
אמר ליה: בבי גזא דרחמנא איתא, דכתיב לה' הארץ ומלואה (= p_bevei_gaza_derachmana)
wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as it is written 'The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness' (Ps 24:1)
ורמי דרבי שמעון בן לקיש אדרבי שמעון בן לקיש... קשיא דריש לקיש אדריש לקיש -- of the hen he says its sanctity lapsed, of the maneh that wherever it is, it is in the treasury

ורמי דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן... קשיא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן; אלא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן קשיא! -- of the hen he says it is in the treasury wherever it is, of the maneh that he is responsible until it reaches the treasurer
R' Yochanan: 'this maneh is for Temple maintenance', and it was stolen or lost -- he bears responsibility for it until it reaches the treasurer
לא קשיא: הא מקמי דשמעיה מרבי יוחנן רביה, הא לבתר דשמעיה -- the hen statement was before he heard it from R' Yochanan his teacher, the maneh statement after (his retraction at 139a.12)
לא קשיא: הא דאמר עלי, הא דאמר הרי זו (= p_ry_alai_veharei_zo)
R' Yochanan's liability for the maneh is where he said 'upon me'; the hen [that stays consecrated] is where he said 'this is'
והתניא: איזהו נדר ואיזו היא נדבה... נדר -- חייב באחריותה -- one who says 'upon me' is responsible
a vow is one who says 'a burnt offering is upon me', a gift one who says 'this is a burnt offering'; a vow that died, was stolen or lost -- he is responsible for it; a gift -- he is not
אמר לך ריש לקיש: הני מילי קדשי מזבח דמחוסר הקרבה (= p_rl_kodshei_mizbeach_bilvad)
that is altar consecrations, which lack sacrifice; but Temple-maintenance consecrations, which do not lack sacrifice -- even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable
והתנן: בית זה עלי קרבן -- נפל הבית -- חייב לשלם -- even of Temple-maintenance consecrations, 'upon me' makes him liable

the mishna: 'this ox is a burnt offering', 'this house is an offering' -- the ox died, the house fell: he is not responsible; 'this ox is upon me as a burnt offering', 'this house is upon me as an offering' -- the ox died, the house fell: he must pay

הני מילי היכא דמת השור ונפל הבית, דליתנהו; אבל היכא דאיתנהו -- כל היכא דאיתיה בבי גזא דרחמנא איתיה -- he pays where the item no longer exists; where it still exists (lost or stolen), it is in the treasury
מתקיף לה רבא: לימא הריני בערכי, הריני בערך פלוני! -- it can be said without 'upon me'
ועוד, תניא, רבי נתן אומר: ונתן את הערכך... חולין עד שיבאו לידי גזבר -- valuation money carries responsibility until it reaches the treasurer

R' Natan: 'and he shall give your valuation on that day, holy to the Lord' (Lev 27:23) -- why stated? since consecrations and tithes redeemed onto non-sacred money carry no responsibility if it is stolen or lost, one might think so here too; the verse says 'and he shall give your valuation' -- it is non-sacred until it reaches the treasurer
בר קטלא הוא -- it is condemned to death [and should have been executed]
rather, a case where its sentence was not passed, and one must bring it to court to fulfil through it 'and you shall eradicate the evil from your midst'
מי מיחייב? כי יקרא קן צפור (Deut 22:6) -- פרט למזומן: even non-sacred, a nest at hand is not subject to sending
a case where he had a nest in his house and consecrated it
ומי קדוש? איש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש (Lev 27:14) -- מה ביתו ברשותו אף כל ברשותו: it is not consecrated at all
a case where he merely saw a nest and consecrated it
האי אפילו בחולין נמי לא מיחייב, דתנא: נטל את הבנים והחזירן לקן... פטור מלשלח (= p_mishna_natal_banim_patur)
a case where he lifted the chicks, consecrated them, and returned them
Rav: [the mishna speaks of] one who consecrates the fruits of his dovecote, and they rebelled
the fruits of his dovecote are altar consecrations; since they are consecrated with inherent sanctity, their sanctity does not lapse from them
by inference, for Reish Lakish, even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable
